sections.title: Venous Thromboembolic Disease (VTE) Overview
content: The most common presentation is Deep vein thrombosis (DVT) of the leg and/or pulmonary embolism (PE).
Deep vein thrombosis (DVT) occurs in 25-50% of surgical patients, and many non-surgical patients.

branches: Patient factors: Increased Age, obesity, varicose veins, previous DVT/PE, family history, pregnancy, oestrogen-containing oral contraceptives & HRT.
Immobility: Especially long flights (> 4 hours) or associated with illness / hospital admission.
Surgical conditions: Recent major surgery (especially pelvic or orthopaedic).
Medical conditions: MI/heart failure, inflammatory bowel disease, pneumonia & malignancy.
Haematological disorders: Thrombophilic states, hyperviscosity syndromes & Myeloproliferative disease.

sections.title: Clinical Signs of DVT
content: Calf warmth, tenderness, swelling, and erythema.
Pitting oedema.
Mild fever.

sections.title: CRITICAL WARNING: Homans' Sign
content: Homans' sign: Increased resistance/pain on forced foot dorsiflexion.
SHOULD NOT BE TESTED: It may dislodge the thrombus.

rows: Usually occurs in patients with rheumatoid arthritis.
Usually distinguished by marked skin erythema & heat localized within a well-demarcated area; may have an entry source (insect bite/ulcer).
Both Ruptured Baker's Cyst and Cellulitis may coexist with a DVT.

sections.title: VTE Investigations
content: 1. FBC: WCC for infection; Hb for polycythaemia; Platelet count for thrombocytosis.
2. D-dimer blood tests: High sensitivity, low specificity (increased in thrombosis, infection, malignancy, and post-op).
3. Compression U/S of calf & leg (Doppler): If negative, repeat at 1 week to catch early propagating DVTs; rules out ruptured knee.
4. Pulmonary Concern: ECG, CXR, ABG, V/Q scan & CT pulmonary angiography.
5. Thrombophilia tests: Before starting anticoagulants if no predisposing factors exist, in recurrent DVT, or strong family history.

sections.title: Complications of VTE
content: 1. Pulmonary embolism: Severity ranges from asymptomatic to sudden death.
2. Chronic post-phlebitic leg problems (10-30%): Due to valve damage; causes pain, swelling, eczema, itch & ulceration.
3. Stroke/Arterial embolus: Paradoxical embolus via cardiac defect.
4. Anticoagulant complications: Haemorrhage (intra-cranial, ocular, GI & other).

sections.title: Prophylaxis against DVT/PE
content: Early post-op mobilization (simplest method).
Compression stockings.
Low M.W heparin (e.g., enoxaparin 20 mg/24h SC).
Aspirin.
Avoid contraceptive pill in high-risk (major/orthopedic surgery).
Vena caval filters (limited use).

sections.title: DVT Management Protocol
content: Step 1: Graded support stockings and treatment of underlying risk factors.
Step 2: Assess risk factors for haemorrhage.
Step 3: Start Heparin (e.g., LMWH enoxaparin 1.5mg/kg/24h SC).
Step 4: Start Warfarin simultaneously with LMWH (prothrombotic for first 48h).
Step 5: Stop heparin when INR reaches 2-3.
Duration: 3 months if post-op; 6 months if no cause found, malignancy, or recurrent DVT.
Vena caval filters: Use in active bleeding or anticoagulant failure to minimize PE risk.

sections.title: WELLS Score: High Probability DVT
content: Calf swelling > 3cm (measured 10cm below tibial tuberosity).
Immobile (bed, plaster, or paralysed).
Local tenderness over deep venous system.
Active malignancy.
Family history of DVT (≥ 2 close relatives).
Others: Pitting edema & dilated superficial veins.

sections.title: Pulmonary Embolism (PE) Essentials
content: Always suspect PE in sudden collapse 1-2 wks after surgery.
Mechanism: Venous thrombi pass into pulmonary circulation and block blood flow.
Signs/Symptoms: Acute dyspnea, tachypnea, pleuritic chest pain, hypotension, tachycardia, gallop rhythm, loud P2, increased JVP, haemoptysis, syncope, Cyanosis, AF, and DVT signs.

rows: Normal/Sinus Tachycardia (commonest). Right ventricular strain (V1-3), Rt Axis deviation, RBBB, AF. Rarely: SI, QIII, TIII (Deep S in I, path. Q in III, inverted T in III).
Often normal. Decreased vascular markings, small pleural effusion, wedge-shaped area of infarction.
Decreased O2, Decreased CO2, Increased pH.
Increased if thrombosis present; helps exclude PE if Normal (High sens/Low spec).
Sensitive & specific for emboli in pulmonary artery. Helical/Spiral CT preferred.
U&E, FBC, baseline clotting. V/Q scan if CTPA unavailable. Pulmonary angiography/venograms if equivocal. Doppler U/S for legs.

sections.title: Immediate PE Management
content: 1. Oxygen 100%.
2. Morphine 10 mg IV (if pain) + antiemetic.
3. If critically ill: Consider immediate thrombolysis or surgery.
4. Start LMWH or Unfractioned Heparin (10,000 U IV bolus then 15–25 U/Kg/h IVI guided by APTT).
5. If Systolic BP > 90 mmHg: Start Warfarin 10 mg/24h PO and confirm diagnosis.
6. If Systolic BP < 90 mmHg: Start rapid colloid infusion (500 mL).
7. Persistent Low BP: Give dobutamine 2.5–10 ug/kg/min IV (Aim BP >90). Consider noradrenaline.
8. Thrombolysis: Consider streptokinase if no improvement after 30–60 min (250,000 U IVI over 30 min, then 100,000 U/h for 12–72 h).

sections.title: Beta-Blocker Clinical Profile
content: Mechanism: Block B-adrenoceptors; B1-blocking is negatively inotropic/chronotropic; B2-blocking induces peripheral vasoconstriction and bronchoconstriction.
Indications: Hypertension (2nd line), IHD (Angina, Post-MI), Cardiac arrhythmias, Hyperthyroidism, Prophylaxis of migraine, Anxiety & tremors, Glaucoma.

Side Effects: Bronchospasm, Hypotension, Bradycardia, Peripheral ischaemia/Cold extremities, Decreased metabolism of other drugs, Potentiation of insulin hypoglycaemia & masking symptoms, Hyperkalaemia (diabetic/uraemic), Nightmares, depression, headache, nausea, vomiting, impotence, possible decreased HDL.

sections.title: BB Bradycardia Antidote & Contraindications
content: Bradycardia Antidote: Atropine up to 3mg IV. If fails, Glucagon 2-10mg IV bolus + 5% dextrose (or 50µg/kg/h infusion). Pacing/Balloon pump if unresponsive.
Contraindications: Congestive heart failure, Heart block, Asthma/COPD, Hypotension & Bradycardia, Prinzmetal's angina, Peripheral vascular disease.

rows: Ascending limb Loop of Henle. Inhibits Na+/K+/2Cl- cotransport.
Acute pulmonary edema, Hypertensive emergencies, Hyper Ca2+ & Hyper K+.
Hypokalaemia, Hypomagnesaemia, Hyponatraemia, Hypocalcaemia, Hyperuricaemia, Ototoxicity.
Proximal part of DCT. Inhibits NaCl cotransport.
Congestive heart failure, Essential hypertension, Diabetes insipidus.
Distal DCT & upper collecting tubules. Competitive inhibition with aldosterone.
Given with other diuretics to balance K+ loss, Hyperaldosteronism.
Hyperkalaemia, Gynecomastia & impotence in males, Menstrual disorders & hirsutism in females.
Nifedipine, Amlodipine, Lacidipine, Nimodipine, Nicardipine, Felodipine
Peripheral V.D, Coronary V.D, Tachycardia (safe with BB), BP lowering.
A-V & S-A conduction delay, Bradycardia (NO BB - risk of LVF), Peripheral & Coronary V.D, BP lowering.

sections.title: CCB Mechanism & Side Effects
content: Mechanism: Block voltage-gated Ca2+ channels in cardiac muscle & vessels. Decreased intracellular Ca2+ reduces muscle contraction, promoting V.D and reducing myocardial oxygen consumption.
Side Effects: CHF aggravation, A-V block, Dizziness, fatigue, headache, flushing, Ankle oedema, Gingival hyperplasia, Nausea, vomiting, constipation.
Contraindications: Heart failure & Heart block.

sections.title: Digitalis (Digoxin) Profile
content: Mechanism: +ve inotropic (blocks Na+/K+ pump), slows HR (control ventricular rate in AF <100), conduction velocity increased in small dose/decreased in large dose.
Indications: CHF with AF (major), heart failure non-responsive to diuretics, atrial flutter, paroxysmal atrial tachycardia.
Dosage: PO loading 0.5mg BID (AF total 1.25-1.5mg in 3-4 doses). Maintenance 0.125-0.25mg daily. IV 0.75-1mg in 0.9% NaCl over 2h.
CI: Digitalis toxicity, Heart block, HOCM, WPW syndrome, Paroxysmal VT.

sections.title: Digitalis Toxicity & Management
content: Precautions: Check K+ levels; lower dose for elderly; halved dose with amiodarone; avoid cardioversion; verify no digitalis in previous 14 days before IV load.
Cardiac SE: Any arrhythmia (AV block, VT/VF).
Ocular SE: White halos, yellow/green chromatopsia, diplopia.
Other SE: Nausea/Vomiting/Anorexia, Hypokalaemia, Digitalis Delirium (Confusion/hallucinations), Gynaecomastia/Galactorrhea.
Management: Stop Digoxin, correct hypokalaemia, treat arrhythmias. Use Digibind® (Digoxin-specific antibody fragments IVI).

rows: Ia: Quinidine, Disopyramide, Procainamide; Ib: Lidocaine; Ic: Flecainide
